newsitem.title: USA: Rubin blasts commission's IRS oversight proposal.
newsitem.headline: Rubin blasts commission's IRS oversight proposal.

text.p: Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin said a national commission's proposal for an independent board to oversee the tax-collecting IRS was "substantially and seriously flawed" and might impede government operations.

Rubin called a news conference hours after the commission issued its report to blast its key recommendation that the Internal Revenue Service be run by a seven-member board drawn mostly from the private sector rather than by Treasury.

"The idea of putting the governance of the IRS in the hands of a private-sector board is a substantially flawed idea with inherent problems that put the functions of the IRS at risk and create conflicts of interest and other problems that make it an unacceptable path to go," Rubin said.

The Treasury Secretary noted that the IRS is the source of 95 percent of the revenues that the federal government takes in, mostly through individual income tax payments, so it was vital that the agency run smoothly.

"I do not think that we can afford to take the risk of a new and untried governing system that, in my judgment, has a substantial chance of not working in respect to an activity that is so central to the functioning of our government," Rubin said.

In addition, there might be at least an appearance of conflict of interest from having private-sector businessmen oversee a tax-collecting agency, Rubin suggested. That would risk undermining taxpayers' sense that they were fairly treated when they made their tax payments.
